decisions.reason: A reference electrometer close to the core dosimetry business costs little to keep and is still featured on the home page in its second year, so the option clearly holds value.

Oncology risk management software builds on the firm's QA platform and its software integration strategy; it keeps a dedicated page and has low marginal carrying cost, so keeping the option open is justified while adoption uncertainty resolves.
A CT image quality phantom launched only in 2024 fits the firm's imaging QA expansion and costs little to maintain, so there is not yet enough evidence to abandon it.
This mammography phantom is distant from the core and overlaps with Product E, which makes consolidation possible, but it is only one year old and cheap to keep, so the option stays open for now.
The full field mammography phantom is new and uncertain but low-cost and supports the firm's move into medical imaging QA, so management keeps it while its market value becomes clearer.
This broad imaging QA instrument line underpins the firm's diversification beyond radiation therapy and has its own page, so it is a strategic option worth keeping.
